title: The Man Who Bought An Entire Bank For $1
sources: BBC News, '1995: Barings Bank collapses' (Barings Bank, founded in 1762, collapsed after Nick Leeson lost 827 million pounds)
The Guardian, 'Dutch bank buys Barings for 1 pound' (ING Group bought Barings Bank on March 6, 1995 for a nominal sum of 1 pound while assuming its liabilities)
The New York Times, 'Barings Sold for One Pound to Dutch Giant'

lines.text: In 1995, a man bought an entire two hundred year old bank
lines.caps: In 1995, | a man bought | an entire | 200 year old | bank

lines.text: And the government let him do it.
See, Barings Bank was one of the most prestigious banks on Earth,
managing money for the Queen of England.
Until one rogue trader in Singapore
secretly gambled away eight hundred million pounds.
The entire bank went bankrupt overnight.
Panicked officials desperately looked for a buyer,
but nobody wanted an eight hundred million dollar debt.
Until a clever Dutch banker stepped up,
handed over a single one-dollar coin,
lines.caps: handed over | a single | one-dollar coin,

lines.text: and walked away owning the entire worldwide empire.
Which proves that with enough debt,
even a royal bank costs less than a cup of coffee.
